prompt: Create one polished desktop website UI design reference, a refined version of the attached existing Vancouver pixel-art portfolio screenshot. Preserve its identity and EXACT background geography: North/West Vancouver below mountains on LEFT, channel in centre, green Lions Gate bridge across centre, wooded Stanley Park continuous with Vancouver downtown on RIGHT. Keep the artwork framing and warm ochre-jacket backpacker on a seawall; NO added foreground trees, no extra bushes, no added buildings. This is a screenshot-like 1440x900 website hero design, not a concept poster. Improve the existing interface into a beautifully restrained pixel-adventure opening: clean muted mint sky; compact header d. danial at top left and Work / About / Say hello top right. In upper sky centred, pixel display headline on two lines 'Taking the' and 'scenic route.' at about 78px desktop, not huge. Short readable sans-serif supporting text 'I’m Danial. I build things, stay curious,' on line 1 and 'and take the scenic route.' on line 2, then one dark forest rectangular CTA 'Start the walk ↓'. No eyebrow above headline, no secondary tiny instructions below it. Landscape should occupy lower 45 percent, broad and clearly visible. Along bottom make a clean narrow off-white pixel-frame journey toolbar: left 'The seawall' with a small '01 / 05'; centre five square numbered checkpoint buttons 01, 02, 03, 04, 05 connected by a dashed trail, captions Start, Shoreline, Lookout, Harbour, Rest. First checkpoint dark green, others off-white with muted green 1px borders. Right outlined 'Still mode Ⅱ'. Enough readable space around controls, no fake stats, no glass, no rounded pills, no gratuitous micro labels. Remove redundant SCROLL TO WANDER bottom text, remove the standalone location-stamp below mountains. Keep the small original 'that’s me!' pointer above character. Retain simple signpost in scenery, forest ink #153e36, paper #f4f4df, mint #b9decf, ochre accents. Art-directed but faithful to original. Render one large clean coherent hero only, readable text, no browser chrome, no extra sections.
